playoff.label: Playoff
summary: Win the Big Ten title and Iowa is in: the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC champions get automatic bids.
Otherwise it needs one of 7 at-large spots. At No. 13 in the committee's ranking it is 9th in line, so 2 of the 8 teams ahead of it need to fall behind it.

games.why: No. 12 Oregon is 1 spot ahead of Iowa in the at-large line. A loss could drop it behind.
No. 10 BYU is 3 spots ahead of Iowa in the at-large line. A loss could drop it behind.

Indiana is ranked behind Iowa, but if it beats Purdue it reaches the Big Ten title game in up to 80 of 128 combinations (none if it loses). Winning that game would give it the automatic bid and put UCLA in the at-large line ahead of Iowa.
No. 8 Wake Forest is 5 spots ahead of Iowa in the at-large line. A loss could drop it behind.
No. 6 Alabama is 7 spots ahead of Iowa in the at-large line. A loss might not drop it far enough, but it would help.
No. 5 Tennessee is 8 spots ahead of Iowa in the at-large line. A loss might not drop it far enough, but it would help.
No. 4 Notre Dame is 9 spots ahead of Iowa in the at-large line. A loss might not drop it far enough, but it would help.
No. 3 Texas is 10 spots ahead of Iowa in the at-large line. A loss might not drop it far enough, but it would help.

playoff.note: Based on this week's committee ranking, which is redone every Tuesday, so a loss by a team ahead doesn't guarantee it drops behind. The field is 12: the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC champions, the highest-ranked team from the other conferences, and the next seven in the ranking. The projected champion of each conference here is simply its highest-ranked team.

title.label: Big Ten title
summary: Iowa reaches the Big Ten title game in 117–150 of the 256 ways the remaining games can finish.

games.why: Iowa reaches the title game in 95–101 of 128 combinations if Purdue wins, and 16–55 of 128 if Indiana wins.
Iowa reaches the title game in 80–102 of 128 combinations if Washington wins, and 37–48 of 128 if Oregon wins.

It depends on Washington at Oregon. If Washington wins, Iowa wants UCLA here (48–64 of 64 combinations against 32–38). If Oregon wins, it wants USC. That game kicks off later, so you won't know yet. Across every result, USC winning is the better bet (64–86 of 128 against 53–64).
Iowa reaches the title game in 68–86 of 128 combinations if Wisconsin wins, and 49–64 of 128 if Minnesota wins.
Iowa reaches the title game in 61–78 of 128 combinations if Michigan wins, and 56–72 of 128 if Ohio State wins.

title.note: Every remaining result counts as equally likely, so these are counts, not odds. They follow the Big Ten's published tiebreaker; ties it can only settle with a ratings service or a draw count as misses. Where a range is shown, the rules can be read two ways: when common opponents are themselves tied in the standings, they don't say whether to compare against those teams one at a time or as a group.
